text:
You helped Tomás go public. Not with a speech, not with a confrontation — with documentation, contacts, the specific and unglamorous work of getting true things into the right hands before anyone could contain them. Tomás had an outside contact from before Aethermoor. You had the archive records. Between you, it was enough.

Solis was gone within two hours of the first disclosure. Personal circumstances, the school said. You were not surprised by the speed.

The school is not in chaos, exactly. Chaos would be simpler. What it's in is the specific institutional unease of a place that has had something true said about it loudly, in public, by people who can substantiate what they're saying. The common rooms are quieter. The faculty corridor is very busy. Nobody stops you in the hall — but everyone is watching.

Ines makes contact three days later. A sealed message, slipped under the door of the library annex where you and Tomás have been spending most of your time. No return address. Her handwriting, which Tomás confirms without speaking.

It reads: "You have no idea what you've done. I chose this. I was safer before you found me."

No signature.

There's no way to know if she means it, or means it the way it sounds, or means something more complicated than either. Tomás reads it four times. Then he folds it and puts it in his wallet, in the place where the other letter used to be.

Lira is gone. Transferred, the school says. Personal circumstances.
